tables.name: booking
tables.purpose: One confirmed purchase: one user, one showtime, one captured payment, one unique customer-facing reference, and a stored total.
tables.cite: E3 P-PAY-01 · E3 P-PAY-10 step 7 · FR-ADR-014 · FR-ADR-039

columns.name: id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 (idempotency_record.id is 'bigint identity') · E6 P-ADM-19 audit_log id table ('bigint identity') · S-XCT-08 ('booking_id 9008')
columns.note: NOT uuid. No document in this project uses a uuid primary key anywhere; the two places a PK type is spelled out both read 'bigint identity', and every id in every criterion and every endpoint body is a small integer (booking_id 9008, user_id 4471, showtime_id 7/41/77, seat_id 312/402). EP-PAY-01's 201 body declares booking_id as 'integer'. The brief's uuid default is overridden here by the sources, as the brief permits.

columns.name: reference
columns.cite: E4 P-TKT-01 · FR-ADR-015 · S-TKT-01
columns.note: THE COLUMN IS NAMED `reference`, not reference_code and not booking_reference. Exactly 8 characters, uppercase, drawn from 23456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ, with NO `FR-` prefix and NO hyphens stored (those are presentation only). `SELECT length(reference), reference = upper(reference) FROM booking WHERE id=:b` must return 8, true. NO CHECK CONSTRAINT ON THE ALPHABET and no length CHECK is added here: OPEN-REFCHAR-01 is reserved (irreversible) and expires at Phase 4; narrowing the alphabet or adding a check character is the client's call. P-TKT-01 states the validation is performed in application code before insert, and that the UNIQUE constraint (not the alphabet) is the guard.

columns.name: user_id
columns.cite: S-ACC-10 (verbatim: 'booking.user_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT') · FR-ADR-014 · E4 EP-TKT-01 authorisation_rule
columns.note: Type spelled `integer` (not bigint) by S-ACC-10. It must match users(id); see notes[] — the merge owner must reconcile this with booking.id being bigint. The owner is always taken from the JWT, never from the request body (S-ACC-10 route-table walk).

columns.name: showtime_id
columns.cite: E7 P-RPT-03 formula ('JOIN booking b ON b.showtime_id = st.id') · S-PAY-06 · S-PAY-15 · EP-PAY-01 201 body
columns.note: Integer, matching E6 P-ADM-14's showtime_seat.showtime_id 'integer'.

columns.name: payment_id
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 ('booking.payment_id points at payment.id, not the reverse') · E3 P-PAY-01 ('no state in which a booking exists without a captured payment') · S-PAY-05 · S-SCP-12 · E7 P-RPT-12
columns.note: THE DIRECTION IS LOAD-BEARING AND SETTLED IN FIVE PLACES. payment carries NO booking_id column: the payment row is inserted at P-PAY-10 step 6 and the booking at step 7, so a payment.booking_id could not be satisfied at insert time. NOT NULL is what makes 'no booking without a payment record' a database fact rather than a test; see gaps[] for the half that is not expressible (the payment being in a terminal captured state).

columns.name: total_paise
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-04 · FR-ADR-039 · S-PAY-01 · S-SEA-16
columns.note: Integer minor unit. The sum of the ALREADY-ROUNDED per-seat prices; the total is never itself rounded. Deliberately denormalised (FR-ADR-039) — the equality total_paise = SUM(booking_seat.price_paise) is asserted at write time as a TEST, explicitly NOT as a database constraint, because a constraint would need a trigger. The minor-unit ratio 100 is CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO, a named configuration value, and appears in no column name, comment or constraint.

columns.name: status
columns.cite: FR-ADR-013 · E3 P-PAY-12 · E7 P-RPT-03 ("b.status = 'confirmed'") · S-PAY-11 · S-SCP-14
columns.note: EXCLUDED IS NOT BLOCKED (SRC-001 §6.6). Written exactly once, by the confirm insert, to 'confirmed'. No v1 endpoint reads or writes it; it appears in no v1 request or response schema. `SELECT DISTINCT status FROM booking` must return exactly one row after the whole suite. TYPE IS UNSOURCED — no document says whether this is a Postgres enum or text, and no document names any value other than 'confirmed'. Declaring an enum here would mean naming a 'cancelled' value, which is the reserved question OPEN-CANCEL-01/OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01. Reported as a gap rather than decided.

columns.name: cancelled_at
columns.cite: FR-ADR-013 · E3 P-PAY-12 · E4 P-TKT-09 · S-PAY-11 · S-SCP-14
columns.note: EXCLUDED IS NOT BLOCKED (SRC-001 §6.6). Stays null for every row v1 ever creates: `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE cancelled_at IS NOT NULL` returns 0. Exists because adding a column to a table already holding real bookings is a migration on live data with a backfill nobody can verify. S-SCP-04 explicitly permits it while banning refund/tax/fee/discount/points/used_at names on this table.

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: E8 P-XCT-04 preconditions ('Every table carries created_at') · S-XCT-08 ('SELECT b.id, b.user_id, b.created_at ...') · S-XCT-09 · E5 P-ACC-11 ordering tie-breaker
columns.note: UTC instant. Serialised to customers with the CINEMA ROW's UTC offset (never Z, never a hardcoded zone) — EP-PAY-01 returns it as created_at, EP-ACC-07 as booked_at. It is also an ordering tie-breaker for the bookings list (S-ACC-12: upcoming ordered by showtime.starts_at asc, booking.created_at desc, booking.id asc).

unique.cite: E4 P-TKT-01 preconditions ('The booking.reference column exists with a UNIQUE constraint on it') · FR-ADR-015 · S-TKT-01
unique.why: The reference is the customer's ONLY proof of purchase and their only way into the hall. Generation draws 8 random characters and RELIES ON THIS CONSTRAINT as the collision guard, retrying up to five times and then failing the request with 500 rather than looping. P-TKT-01: 'The arithmetic is not the guard; the constraint is.'

foreign_keys.note: Red-proofed: the constraint is temporarily redefined CASCADE, the delete is watched destroying the booking and its snapshotted prices, then restored to RESTRICT and the restore verified. DELETE FROM users with a booking present must raise SQLSTATE 23503.

foreign_keys.cite: S-XCT-09 ('SELECT conname, confdeltype FROM pg_constraint WHERE contype = \'f\' AND confdeltype <> \'r\' returns 0 rows')
E3 P-PAY-07 · E7 P-RPT-12 ('The join runs payment.id = booking.payment_id, not the reverse') · S-XCT-09

indexes.why: The dashboard aggregate drives from showtime, filtered by period and screen, then joins booking on showtime_id. Named as a required index by the PRD and asserted by S-RPT-16 against pg_indexes.
The takings query joins payment on p.id = b.payment_id.

tables.name: booking_seat
tables.purpose: One row per booked seat: the seat-occupancy record that carries the oversell guard and the immutable per-seat price snapshot.
tables.cite: FR-ADR-024 ('The unique constraint is declared on the seat-occupancy table — one row per (booking, seat)') · FR-ADR-039 · E3 P-PAY-05

columns.name: id
columns.cite: project id convention: FR-ADR-020, E6 P-ADM-19 ('bigint identity')
columns.note: NO DOCUMENT NAMES A PRIMARY KEY FOR THIS TABLE. See gaps[] — the merge owner must choose between a surrogate id and a composite PK on (booking_id, seat_id). Nothing in any criterion selects a booking_seat id.

columns.name: booking_id
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-10 step 7 · S-PAY-03 · S-PAY-07 · S-SCP-13 · S-XCT-08 · E7 P-RPT-03 formula
columns.note: Every criterion in the Bible that reads a booked seat filters on booking_id.

columns.name: showtime_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-024 · E3 P-PAY-11 · S-XCT-01 · S-XCT-02 · S-XCT-03 · S-PAY-09 · S-SEA-13 · S-SEA-16 · S-SEA-18 · S-SEA-20
columns.note: DENORMALISED FROM booking.showtime_id ON PURPOSE. It exists so the oversell unique constraint can be (showtime_id, seat_id) — the guarantee has to be at seat granularity across the whole showtime, not per booking. At least nine acceptance criteria run `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=? AND seat_id=?` directly. Nothing in the documents states how showtime_id is kept consistent with booking.showtime_id.

columns.name: seat_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-024 · S-PAY-09 ('seat_id is an integer foreign key and seat_label carries the human form such as F7; a query comparing seat_id to a label string raises invalid input syntax for type integer against a correct schema') · S-XCT-08 · S-XCT-34
columns.note: INTEGER, NOT A LABEL. The human-readable form (F7, C12) lives on the `seat` table and is joined for display (S-XCT-08: `JOIN seat s ON s.id = bs.seat_id`); it is never copied onto booking_seat.

columns.name: price_paise
columns.cite: FR-ADR-039 · E3 P-PAY-05 · S-PAY-01 · S-SEA-16 · E7 P-RPT-03
columns.note: The rounded per-seat price the customer actually paid, snapshotted at HOLD acquisition (not at confirm) and copied onto this row; never recomputed by any display path, receipt, bookings list or dashboard. Integer minor unit, bigint.

columns.name: base_price_paise_applied
columns.cite: FR-ADR-039 · E3 P-PAY-05 (column table) · S-PAY-03 · S-SEA-16
columns.note: The showtime base price that produced price_paise. Stored so the figure is auditable — SRC-001 §7.6 requires the system to answer for its own records; storing only price_paise makes it impossible to tell a 33.33% uplift on Rs 275.00 from a 20% uplift on something else. Money column: bigint, name ends _paise.

columns.name: uplift_basis_points_applied
columns.cite: FR-ADR-039 · E3 P-PAY-05 (column table) · S-PAY-03 · S-SEA-16
columns.note: The seat category's uplift in basis points at the time of booking. NOT a money column — its name deliberately does not end in _paise, and S-PAY-01's assertion (money columns on booking/booking_seat/payment ending in _paise are EXACTLY total_paise, price_paise, base_price_paise_applied, amount_paise) depends on that.

columns.name: seat_category_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-039 ('the category at the time of booking, copied, not joined for display') · E3 P-PAY-05 ('integer, positive, non-null') · S-PAY-03
columns.note: Copied rather than joined, so a later category rename or re-categorisation cannot rewrite what a past receipt says.

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: E8 P-XCT-04 ('Every table carries created_at') · S-XCT-09
columns.note: S-XCT-09 asserts information_schema returns zero public tables lacking created_at.

unique.why: THE PRODUCT. The second half of the double-booking guarantee, and the half that may not be waived at any confidence for any reason (waiving a quality check is reserved to the client, CONSTITUTION Art III.8). TOTAL, NOT PARTIAL — the documents settle this explicitly and in five places. FR-ADR-024: 'The constraint is total, not partial. No WHERE status <> cancelled clause.' P-PAY-11: 'The constraint is total, not partial. There is no WHERE status <> cancelled clause, because P-PAY-12 rules out cancellation in v1. If cancellation is ever added, this constraint has to be revisited first — a cancelled booking holding a seat forever is what a total constraint would then produce.' Three criteria assert the absence of a WHERE clause directly against the catalogue: S-XCT-02 and S-XCT-03 read pg_get_constraintdef and require no WHERE; S-XCT-04 requires `SELECT indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'booking_seat'` to contain no WHERE and requires the guard to be a CONSTRAINT rather than a partial index; S-PAY-09 requires pg_indexes to return EXACTLY ONE unique index on this table. So a cancelled booking's seats are NOT freed, and that is the ruled behaviour, not an oversight. It must be created in the SAME Alembic revision as create_table('booking_seat') (S-XCT-04), so no window exists in which a seat row can be written without it, and no later revision may drop it.

foreign_keys.cite: S-XCT-08 ('JOIN seat s ON s.id = bs.seat_id') · S-XCT-34 · S-XCT-09
foreign_keys.note: S-XCT-09's blanket rule: every FK on a path that can reach a booking is ON DELETE RESTRICT; `SELECT conname, confdeltype FROM pg_constraint WHERE contype='f' AND confdeltype <> 'r'` returns 0 rows. Note that DELETE /api/admin/seats/{seat_id} exists but is permitted only while the hall has no showtime rows at all, so it is unreachable from a booking.

UNCERTAIN — no document states that this FK exists, only what its on_delete would have to be if it does. See gaps[]: the alternative is a composite FK to showtime_seat(showtime_id, seat_id), which would additionally guarantee the booked seat is actually on that showtime. Do not treat this row as sourced.

indexes.why: Every read of a booking's seats — the receipt, the bookings list, the confirmation page, the takings sum — joins booking_seat on booking_id.

tables.name: payment
tables.purpose: One row per booking ATTEMPT recording the simulated provider's state machine, the amount captured, the transition instants, and the idempotency key that produced it.

columns.name: id
columns.cite: project id convention: FR-ADR-020, E6 P-ADM-19 ('bigint identity') · referenced by booking.payment_id
columns.note: The payment row is inserted BEFORE the booking row (P-PAY-10 step 6 then step 7), so its id must be available to the booking insert.

columns.name: state
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 · FR-ADR-041 · E7 P-RPT-03 ('payment.state is one of pending, authorized, captured, failed') · S-PAY-11 ('SELECT unnest(enum_range(NULL::payment_state))') · S-SCP-12 ('the column is state')
columns.note: THE COLUMN IS NAMED `state`, NOT `status`. Two Bible criteria get this wrong — see notes[]. It is a real Postgres enum type named payment_state: S-PAY-11 asserts `enum_range(NULL::payment_state)` returns exactly four rows and no 'refunded'. Transitions are enforced in code: capture from pending is rejected (InvalidPaymentTransition), and failed is terminal.

columns.name: amount_paise
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 ('carrying the state, the amount in paise, the transition timestamps and the Idempotency-Key') · FR-ADR-041 · S-PAY-01 · S-PAY-05 · S-PAY-10
columns.note: The fourth and last money column in this cluster. S-PAY-10: payment.amount_paise, booking.total_paise and the figure on the checkout total are all the same integer, and `SELECT sum(price_paise) FROM booking_seat WHERE booking_id=B` also returns it. Never a float, never NUMERIC(x,2).

columns.name: idempotency_key
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 ('One payment row per booking attempt, carrying ... the Idempotency-Key that produced it') · FR-ADR-041 · S-PAY-05 · S-PAY-15
columns.note: NOT UNIQUE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. S-PAY-15 proves it: the same FAIL_-prefixed key sent twice leaves `SELECT count(*) FROM payment WHERE state='failed'` at 2 — two payment rows share one key, because each failed attempt commits its own row in its own transaction while the booking transaction (and its idempotency_record row) rolls back. Putting a unique constraint here would break the deliberate fail->retry->succeed drill. The idempotency guard lives on idempotency_record, not here.

columns.name: pending_at
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 happy path step 1 ('Insert a payment row in pending') · S-PAY-05 · S-SCP-12 ('pending_at <= authorized_at <= captured_at')
columns.note: The row is always created in pending, so this is always set.

columns.name: authorized_at
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 happy path step 3 ('Transition to authorized, then to captured, recording each timestamp') · S-PAY-05 · S-SCP-12
columns.note: Null while pending and on a failed row that never authorised. American spelling `authorized` throughout the documents (matching the enum value), not `authorised`.

columns.name: captured_at
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 happy path step 3 · S-PAY-05 ('SELECT state, captured_at FROM payment WHERE id=P still returns pending and null')
columns.note: Null unless the row reached captured. Likely the source of EP-TKT-01's `paid_at` wire field — see gaps[].

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: E8 P-XCT-04 ('Every table carries created_at') · S-XCT-09
columns.note: Required by the blanket rule even though pending_at will normally hold the same instant.

indexes.why: Every takings and dashboard aggregate filters `p.state = 'captured'`.

tables.name: idempotency_record
tables.purpose: The per-user idempotency guard for booking confirmation: inserted first, inside the booking transaction, so two simultaneous retries collide in the database rather than both booking.

columns.name: id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 column table (verbatim: 'id | bigint identity')
columns.note: The one place in this cluster where a primary key type is spelled out in a source document.

columns.name: user_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('non-null foreign key. The key is scoped per user') · E3 P-PAY-09 ('Scope is per user')
columns.note: SCOPE IS PER USER, NOT GLOBAL. P-PAY-09: 'Two customers can generate the same key — a weak client generator, or a copied request — and a global scope would hand one of them the other's booking.' S-PAY-06 asserts the same key from a different user id inserts cleanly and confirms normally. Type follows booking.user_id / users(id).

columns.name: idempotency_key
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('the client''s header value, text') · E3 P-PAY-09 · EP-PAY-01 headers · S-PAY-06
columns.note: 1..255 characters, REQUIRED — a missing header is 400 REQUEST_INVALID, never a permitted omission. Compared as an EXACT BYTE SEQUENCE: never trimmed, lowercased, casefolded or unicode-normalised. S-PAY-06 proves it by inserting a key, the same key with one trailing space, and the same key uppercased, and asserting three rows. The value is minted by the CLIENT (crypto.randomUUID(), 36 chars, 122 random bits), once per confirm attempt, never by the server.

columns.name: request_fingerprint
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('a hash of the canonicalised request body') · E3 P-PAY-09
columns.note: For EP-PAY-01 the canonicalised body is hold_token + showtime_id. A same-key request whose fingerprint differs is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, permanently, because the record is never deleted.

columns.name: status
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('status | in_progress or completed') · E3 P-PAY-09
columns.note: TYPE NAME IS UNSOURCED. The two values are a closed, fully documented set, but no document says whether the SQL type is a Postgres enum or text — payment_state is the only type in this cluster the Bible pins as an enum (S-PAY-11). The enum name here is a placeholder the merge owner may replace with text.

columns.name: booking_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('nullable foreign key, set when the booking commits') · E3 P-PAY-09 happy path step 4 · E3 P-PAY-10 step 11
columns.note: Null while in_progress; written at step 11 together with response_body and status='completed'.

columns.name: response_body
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('jsonb, the response that was returned') · E3 P-PAY-09 · S-PAY-06
columns.note: Returned BYTE FOR BYTE to a duplicate whose winner is completed — never a second booking and never a second capture. Null while in_progress.

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('created_at, completed_at | timestamptz') · E8 P-XCT-04 · S-XCT-09

columns.name: completed_at
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('created_at, completed_at | timestamptz') · E3 P-PAY-09
columns.note: Null while in_progress.

unique.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('Unique constraint on (user_id, idempotency_key)') · E3 P-PAY-09 · EP-PAY-01 idempotency block · S-PAY-06
unique.why: THE CHECK AND THE ACT IN ONE STATEMENT. The row is inserted FIRST, in the same transaction as the booking, before any other work. The insert either succeeds — this request owns the key — or it violates the constraint, in which case this request is a duplicate. There is no check-then-act window, which is exactly the trap GOTCHAS.md records: 'An idempotency key stored after the work is done is not idempotent. Two simultaneous retries both check, both find nothing, both book.' The three duplicate behaviours are the whole set: winner completed -> replay the stored response_body with the original status code; winner in_progress -> 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT with Retry-After (never a wait, because holding a connection open ties up one of ~110 on a db.t3.micro); fingerprint differs -> 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.

foreign_keys.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('non-null foreign key') · S-XCT-09 (blanket RESTRICT rule)
FR-ADR-020 ('nullable foreign key, set when the booking commits') · S-XCT-09

enums.name: payment_state
enums.cite: FR-ADR-041 · E3 P-PAY-07 · E3 P-PAY-12 · E7 P-RPT-03 · S-PAY-11 ('SELECT unnest(enum_range(NULL::payment_state)) returns those four rows and no refunded value')
enums.note: THERE IS NO `refunded` VALUE AND NONE MAY BE ADDED — P-PAY-12 is reserved: money. A captured simulated payment is never unwound: no refund table, no refund amount column, no cancellation reason, no cancellation-policy configuration. `failed` is terminal. Spelling is American (`authorized`) in every source.

enums.name: idempotency_status
enums.note: UNSOURCED TYPE NAME — see the column note. The value set is closed and documented; only the SQL type and its name are not.

gaps.what: `paid_at` is returned by EP-TKT-01 but no document names a column for it.
gaps.why_it_matters: EP-TKT-01's 200 body declares `paid_at` (ISO-8601 with the cinema's UTC offset) and P-TKT-09 happy path step 4 says the response carries 'the instant payment was captured'. S-TKT-03 asserts the body's key set is exactly reference, film_title, hall_name, starts_at, seats, total_paise, paid_at, receipt_email_address — so the field ships. The obvious read is that it is serialised from payment.captured_at through booking.payment_id, and NO booking.paid_at column is created here. If the merge owner instead adds a booking.paid_at column, it duplicates payment.captured_at and creates two instants that can disagree. Naming which one it is, is a one-line decision that nobody has recorded.
gaps.where_you_looked: docs/03 PRD/sections/E4_receipt_entry.md P-TKT-03, P-TKT-09, EP-TKT-01; E3 P-PAY-07 and P-PAY-10; grep for paid_at across docs/03 PRD/sections and the Bible CSV (4 hits, all wire-level).

gaps.what: `booking.status` — no document states the SQL type or the full value set. Only 'confirmed' is ever named.
gaps.why_it_matters: E7 P-RPT-03's takings query hard-codes `b.status = 'confirmed'` and S-SCP-14 asserts `SELECT DISTINCT status FROM booking` returns exactly one row. But payment_state is declared a Postgres enum and booking.status is not, and nothing names a second value. Declaring an enum would require naming a 'cancelled' value, which answers OPEN-CANCEL-01 / OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01 (both reserved). Declaring text leaves the column unconstrained. The merge owner must pick a type; picking the VALUE SET is not theirs.
gaps.where_you_looked: FR-ADR-013 in full; E3 P-PAY-12; E7 P-RPT-03; grep for booking_status and enum_range across the PRD, the ADRs and the Bible CSV — enum_range appears exactly once and only for payment_state.

gaps.what: `idempotency_record` stores no HTTP status code, but P-PAY-09 requires a replay to return 'the original status code'.
gaps.why_it_matters: FR-ADR-020's column table and P-PAY-09's prose both enumerate the columns and neither includes a status-code column; exception 3 nonetheless says 'The stored response_body and the original status code, byte for byte' and S-PAY-06 asserts 'the second response is byte-for-byte the stored response_body with the original 201 status'. Today the only outcome that ever reaches status='completed' is a 201, so a constant works — but the contract is written as though the code were stored. Either add the column or write down that 201 is the only completable outcome. Do not guess.
gaps.where_you_looked: docs/01 ADR/all-ADRs/FR-ADR-020.md column table; docs/03 PRD/sections/E3_checkout_payment.md P-PAY-09 (behaviour paragraph, exception 3, EP-PAY-01 idempotency block); Bible S-PAY-06.

gaps.what: `payment` records no instant of failure — there is no `failed_at`.
gaps.why_it_matters: P-PAY-07 says the row carries 'the transition timestamps' and names pending_at, authorized_at and captured_at through S-PAY-05 and S-SCP-12. `failed` is a state the documents deliberately made observable by committing it in its own transaction ('The separate commit is what makes failed mean anything'), yet nothing records WHEN it failed — only created_at/pending_at. An operator asked how many captures failed in an hour has no column to filter on.
gaps.where_you_looked: E3 P-PAY-07 in full, FR-ADR-041, Bible S-PAY-05 / S-PAY-15 / S-SCP-12; grep for failed_at across docs/03 PRD/sections, docs/01 ADR and the Bible CSV — zero hits.

gaps.why_it_matters: FR-ADR-024 says only 'one row per (booking, seat)'. No criterion ever selects a booking_seat id. The choice is between a surrogate bigint identity and a composite PK on (booking_id, seat_id). The composite would add a second uniqueness guarantee (the same seat cannot appear twice in one booking) that nothing currently provides; the surrogate would not. Neither is stated.
gaps.where_you_looked: FR-ADR-024, FR-ADR-039, E3 P-PAY-05, E3 P-PAY-10 step 7, every Bible criterion touching booking_seat.

gaps.what: Nothing guarantees that a `booking_seat` row's seat is actually on its showtime, and no document names the foreign key on booking_seat.showtime_id.
gaps.why_it_matters: booking_seat carries showtime_id and seat_id independently. E6 P-ADM-14 materialises the exact seat set of a showtime into `showtime_seat` with its own UNIQUE (showtime_id, seat_id). A composite FK from booking_seat(showtime_id, seat_id) to showtime_seat(showtime_id, seat_id) would make 'a seat you booked was on that show' a database fact; a plain FK to showtime(id) would not. The documents describe both tables carefully and never connect them, and E6 explicitly warns that 'a reader who conflates them will believe the oversell guard has been moved'. This is a real modelling choice with real consequences and no source settles it.
gaps.where_you_looked: docs/03 PRD/sections/E6_admin.md P-ADM-14 (lines ~1920-2014), FR-ADR-024, E3 P-PAY-10/P-PAY-11, S-XCT-09's blanket FK rule, grep for showtime_seat across the PRD.

gaps.what: 'No booking exists without a payment record in a terminal captured state' is only half expressible as a constraint.
gaps.why_it_matters: P-PAY-01 states it absolutely: 'A booking row exists only after a payment record for it has reached the captured state ... no state in which a booking exists without a captured payment.' `booking.payment_id NOT NULL` makes the EXISTENCE half a database fact. The STATE half — that the referenced payment is 'captured' — cannot be expressed without a trigger or a redundant denormalised copy of state onto booking, and no document authorises either. FR-ADR-039 has already ruled the analogous total==sum assertion 'a test, not a database constraint — a constraint would need a trigger', so the same answer probably applies, but nobody wrote it down for this one. Flagging it because the goal names this invariant as runnable.

gaps.what: `updated_at`: E8 P-XCT-04 requires 'tables that mutate carry updated_at', and the criteria contradict it.
gaps.why_it_matters: payment mutates (pending -> authorized -> captured) and idempotency_record mutates (in_progress -> completed), so the rule would put updated_at on both. But no criterion in the Bible ever selects or asserts an updated_at on either, and S-ACC-01 pins the users table's column list as 'exactly id, email, password_hash, role, password_version, created_at, last_signed_in_at and nothing else' — users mutates and has no updated_at. The rule is therefore already false somewhere. NO updated_at COLUMN IS ADDED IN THIS OUTPUT. The merge owner must decide whether P-XCT-04's sentence is a schema rule or a stale generality, and it has to be answered once for all six clusters.
gaps.where_you_looked: docs/03 PRD/sections/E8_crosscutting.md P-XCT-04 preconditions (line 307); S-XCT-09's information_schema assertion, which demands created_at only; Bible S-ACC-01, S-PAY-05, S-PAY-06.

gaps.what: Integer width is inconsistent across the id chain: booking.user_id is spelled `integer` while primary keys are spelled `bigint identity`.
gaps.why_it_matters: S-ACC-10 quotes the migration verbatim: 'booking.user_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)'. FR-ADR-020 and E6 P-ADM-19 both spell a primary key 'bigint identity'. A foreign key must match its target's type, so either users.id is integer (and the bigint-identity convention does not apply to users) or S-ACC-10's wording is loose. Resolved by the users-cluster owner, not here; recorded so the merge does not silently pick one.
gaps.where_you_looked: Bible S-ACC-10 and S-ACC-01; FR-ADR-020; docs/03 PRD/sections/E6_admin.md audit_log column table (line ~2429); EP-PAY-01's 201 body ('booking_id: integer').

gaps.what: Retention of booking, booking_seat, payment and idempotency_record is ruled 'never deleted' but the underlying legal question is still open.
gaps.why_it_matters: FR-ADR-012 and P-PAY-09 rule that the idempotency record is never expired and never deleted ('A key that expires is a key whose retry after the window creates a second booking'), and S-XCT-09 asserts no DELETE statement exists against any of these tables and no scheduled pruning exists. But OPEN-OPS-02 — 'How long must booking records be kept? A retention floor is a legal question and a storage cost' — is still OPEN and reserved: legal in CONSTITUTION Article X. The schema is correct today; the row is named here so nobody reads 'never deleted' as a closed question.

notes: PRIMARY KEYS ARE NOT UUID IN THIS PROJECT. The brief's default says uuid; the sources disagree and I followed the sources, as the brief permits. Two documents spell a primary key out and both read 'bigint identity' (FR-ADR-020's idempotency_record column table; E6 P-ADM-19's audit_log column table). Every identifier in every acceptance criterion and every endpoint body is a small integer — booking_id 9008, user_id 4471, showtime_id 7/41/77, seat_id 312/402 — and EP-PAY-01's 201 body declares booking_id and showtime_id as 'integer'. FR-ADR-015 additionally REJECTS a UUID by name, though for the customer-facing reference rather than the PK. The ids are database-generated identity, not application-generated. If any other cluster reader returned uuid PKs, this is a merge conflict that has to be settled before schema.sql is written.

TWO ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA CONTAIN SQL THAT CANNOT RUN AGAINST A CORRECT SCHEMA, AND BOTH FAIL THE SAME WAY. S-XCT-32 (Keep every container stateless) runs `SELECT count(*) FROM booking b LEFT JOIN payment p ON p.booking_id = b.id WHERE p.id IS NULL`, and S-XCT-45 (the seed) runs `SELECT count(*) FROM booking b LEFT JOIN payment p ON p.booking_id = b.id WHERE p.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'captured'`. `payment.booking_id` does not exist — S-PAY-05 asserts `SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns ... column_name='booking_id'` returns 0 and S-SCP-12 restates it, and the direction is argued from ordering in five places (the payment row is inserted at P-PAY-10 step 6, the booking at step 7, so a payment.booking_id could not be satisfied at insert time). S-XCT-45 additionally names `payment.status`; the column is `payment.state` (S-SCP-12: 'the column is state'). Both criteria will raise UndefinedColumn. Their INTENT is right and is already guaranteed by `booking.payment_id NOT NULL`. Corrected forms are given in sql_seen_in_criteria. This is a Bible defect to file, not a schema change.

THE LIKELY ORIGIN OF THAT DEFECT IS FR-ADR-041, WHICH SAYS 'A payment row, one per booking'. E3 P-PAY-07 says 'One payment row per booking attempt', and S-PAY-15 proves the second reading is the right one: two failed attempts leave two payment rows and zero bookings. A failed payment has no booking at all. Anyone writing SQL from FR-ADR-041's sentence will reach for payment.booking_id, which is exactly what happened twice. Worth a one-line erratum on the ADR.

THE UNIQUE CONSTRAINT QUESTION IS SETTLED, NOT OPEN, AND THE ANSWER IS 'TOTAL'. I looked for a partial index and there is none: FR-ADR-024 ('The constraint is total, not partial. No WHERE status <> cancelled clause'), P-PAY-11 ('The constraint is total, not partial'), and three separate criteria that read the catalogue back and require no WHERE clause (S-XCT-02, S-XCT-03, S-XCT-04) plus one that requires exactly one unique index on booking_seat (S-PAY-09). The consequence is stated and accepted: a cancelled booking's seats would NOT be freed. Both records carry the same revisit trigger in the same words — 'If cancellation is ever added, this constraint has to be revisited FIRST, because a cancelled booking holding a seat forever is what a total constraint would then produce.' That sentence should survive into schema.sql as a comment; it is the one thing a future migration author must read before touching this table.

THE CONSTRAINT MUST BE CREATED IN THE SAME ALEMBIC REVISION AS create_table('booking_seat') (S-XCT-04), so that no revision exists in which a seat row could be written without it, and `rg -in 'drop_constraint|DROP CONSTRAINT' backend/migrations` must return 0 hits up to head. The only DROP that is permitted is the one the red-proof drill (S-XCT-02) performs by hand against a loopback-only local stack, and it is restored and the restore is verified.

HOLDS HAVE NO TABLE AND I MODELLED NONE. S-PAY-08 asserts `SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_name IN ('seat_hold','hold','seat_lock','lock')` returns 0 — 'there is no PostgreSQL table a hold check could fall back to'. The per-seat price snapshot that lands on booking_seat is taken at HOLD acquisition and lives in the Redis hold value until confirm reads it (P-PAY-05, S-SEA-16, S-ADM-15). OPEN-HOLDRECOVER-01 is reserved: scope.

NO CARD DATA WAS FOUND ANYWHERE, AND I LOOKED. No column, no comment, no example, no fixture reference in any document. P-PAY-08 forbids it explicitly and S-SCP-12 greps for card_?number|pan|cvv|cvc|expiry|expiration|cardholder across backend/app, backend/migrations, frontend/src, scripts AND backend/tests, requiring 0 hits. It also bans stripe|razorpay|payu|paypal|braintree|adyen. Nothing card-shaped exists to report as a defect.

MONEY: exactly four columns across this cluster end in _paise — booking.total_paise, booking_seat.price_paise, booking_seat.base_price_paise_applied and payment.amount_paise — all bigint, and S-PAY-01 asserts that list is EXACTLY complete for booking+booking_seat+payment. booking_seat.uplift_basis_points_applied is a basis-point integer and deliberately does NOT carry the suffix. The minor-unit ratio (100) is the named configuration value CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO and appears in no column name, no comment and no constraint; `currency_code` is likewise configuration (CURRENCY_CODE) and is NOT a column — EP-PAY-01 returns it in the 201 body but no criterion reads it from a table. S-XCT-05 requires `SELECT SUM(price_paise)` to be cast back to BigInteger inside the query, because SUM over bigint returns numeric and arrives in Python as Decimal — GOTCHAS.md records this and E7 P-RPT-03 names it as one of four load-bearing things in the takings query.

THE THREE TRANSACTION FACTS THE MERGE OWNER NEEDS. (1) One PostgreSQL transaction at READ COMMITTED — the constraint holds at every isolation level and SERIALIZABLE is explicitly rejected (P-PAY-10). (2) Order inside the transaction: idempotency_record insert, Redis hold re-validation, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the showtime row, showtime read, price sum from the hold snapshot, payment insert+capture, booking + booking_seat insert, audit no-op, receipt_dispatch insert, outbox_message insert, idempotency_record -> completed, COMMIT. S-PAY-07 asserts that exact order from an instrumented run. (3) SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is taken ONLY on the showtime row and never to test whether a seat is free — `rg -n 'FOR UPDATE' backend/app/api/bookings.py` must return exactly one hit and that line must also match 'showtime'. A row lock cannot protect a row that does not exist yet.

COLUMN-NAME TRAPS THAT WILL BREAK TESTS IF THE MERGE GETS THEM WRONG: the booking reference column is `reference` (NOT reference_code, NOT booking_reference — those are the WIRE field names); the payment state column is `state` (NOT status); the booking state column is `status` (NOT state); payment has NO booking_id; booking_seat has NO seat_label (the label lives on `seat` and is joined); the price-input columns carry the `_applied` suffix (base_price_paise_applied, uplift_basis_points_applied) and dropping it fails S-PAY-03.

TABLE NAMES: I did not rename anything and none of the four looks wrong. Note however that `idempotency_record` NEVER APPEARS BY THAT NAME ANYWHERE IN THE PRD — grep for it across docs/03 PRD/sections returns zero hits; P-PAY-09 and FR-ADR-020 only ever say 'the idempotency record' or 'a table in PostgreSQL'. The name comes solely from the Bible criteria (S-PAY-06, S-PAY-07, S-PAY-15) and the brief's fixed list. Those criteria are enough to fix it, but the PRD should be made to say the name out loud.

NO CHECK CONSTRAINTS ARE PROPOSED ON ANY OF THE FOUR TABLES, AND EACH OMISSION IS DELIBERATE. (a) No alphabet or length CHECK on booking.reference — OPEN-REFCHAR-01 is reserved (irreversible) and expires at the first confirmed booking in Phase 4; P-TKT-01 puts the validation in application code and names the UNIQUE constraint as the guard. (b) No CHECK that booking.total_paise equals SUM(booking_seat.price_paise) — FR-ADR-039 rules in terms that this 'is a test, not a database constraint — a constraint would need a trigger', and P-PAY-04 repeats it. (c) No CHECK that booking.payment_id's row is in state 'captured' — same trigger problem, see gaps[]. (d) No CHECK on total_paise > 0 — P-PAY-04 states it as SERVER-SIDE validation, not as a database constraint, and adopting it as a CHECK would be stricter than the document rather than equal to it; flagged for the merge owner rather than taken. (e) No redemption, admission, scanned, checked_in or entry column and no CHECK about one — S-TKT-12 asserts all five names are absent, and adding one would answer OPEN-DUPREF-01, reserved: product.

P-XCT-04's 'tables that mutate carry updated_at' is the one cross-cutting schema rule I declined to apply, and the reason is in gaps[]: no criterion anywhere asserts an updated_at, and S-ACC-01 pins the users column list with none. It has to be answered once, for all six clusters, by the merge owner.
